## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@bfb230b23ae0b0a6f0e87800894a9b86e741e87e
    with:
      runtime_ref: bfb230b23ae0b0a6f0e87800894a9b86e741e87e

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@bfb230b23ae0b0a6f0e87800894a9b86e741e87e
    with:
      runtime_ref: bfb230b23ae0b0a6f0e87800894a9b86e741e87e
      issue_number: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}

Core:

  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element

  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page

We need to build a complete playable 3D Mario Kart-style racing game with turbo boost. Empty repo. Plan: static HTML/JS game using Three.js. Can we use npm? There's no package.json; static html type. We can include Three.js locally. Network access? Let's test npm availability and internet. We could use CDN import, but offline capture may fail. Better download three.module.js locally to vendor. Check network.

Let's think about game design deeply to make quality.

Game: "Turbo Karts" 3D racing, Mario Kart style:
- Kart physics on a track with curves (a spline-based closed circuit).
- Drift mechanic: hold drift while turning, build mini-turbo charge, release for boost (blue/orange sparks).
- Turbo pads on track, item boxes maybe.
- AI opponents (4-6 karts) following racing line with rubber-banding.
- 3 laps, lap timer, positions, speedometer, boost meter.
- Visual: colorful low-poly world, sky gradient, grandstands, trees, coins? Use Three.js primitives + generated textures/canvas.
- Mobile touch controls: steering buttons left/right, accelerate, brake, drift, plus tilt optional? Keep on-screen controls, responsive.
- Sound: WebAudio engine sound synthesized, boost whoosh, countdown beeps. Need user gesture start.
- Screens: title/start screen with kart selection maybe, HUD, pause, results. Keyboard WASD/arrows, Space drift, Shift boost? Classic: Space drift. R to reset, Esc pause.
- Turbo boost: drift mini-turbo tiers; also boost pads; maybe manual "boost" via meter filled by drifting? Request specifically "с турбо-ускорением" so make prominent: boost gauge fills from drifting and tricks/pads; press Shift or on-screen TURBO button to activate.

Better: boost meter that fills with drifting, boost pads and airtime; press Shift to spend. Plus drift mini-turbo. That gives accessible turbo.

Track: Build from CatmullRomCurve3 closed with elevation, create road mesh ribbon with width ~14, plus edges/curbs. Need robust kart physics: simplest arcade approach: move freely on plane with steering and speed, constrain to track via nearest point on curve; off-road slows. But for good feel and to prevent falling, use projected track parameter for AI and player: player free movement with collision against track boundaries? Simpler approach: 2.5D track-surface projection: Compute nearest point on centerline; allow lateral offset within road half-width + shoulder; if beyond, slow and clamp. Height from centerline interpolation + banking. Kart yaw independent. This is reliable and avoids physics complexity.

However 3D track with elevation and kart following terrain: compute y from nearest point on spline, plus normal orientation. For mesh, generate ribbon along curve using Frenet frames with up vector fixed to avoid twisting.

Track design: fun circuit with hairpin, sweeping turns, elevation changes, loop? Not a loop (would complicate). Use points defining shape e.g.:
(0,0,0), (60,0,-30), (120,0,0), (160,10,-60), (120,20,-120), (40,14,-140), (0,6,-90), (-60,4,-120), (-120,10,-80), (-140,0,-10), (-90,-2,40), (-20,0,50), (30,2,30). Need ensure no self intersection and nice width. Let me design more carefully later with validation (check min distance between non-adjacent samples > road width).

Visual style: vibrant "sunset carnival" or "Mario" style with green hills, floating clouds, colorful banners, palm trees, mushroom-like trees. Use procedural textures on road (canvas with asphalt noise + dashed center line + checkered start). Curbs red/white striped via geometry segments alternating colors.

Karts: low-poly cartoon karts: chassis box, rounded nose, spoiler, 4 wheels (cylinders), driver capsule with helmet, exhaust pipes. Colors per racer. Wheels spin, front wheels steer, body tilts/rolls in turns, suspension bounce. Boost flames from exhaust when boosting. Drift sparks particles at rear wheels colored by charge tier.

AI: follow racing line offset with target speed based on curvature; steer smoothly; drift visually; use boost on straights occasionally. Rubber band distance-based speed adjustments. Position ranking by lap + progress. Avoidance: lateral offsets.

Items? Mario Kart style implies maybe item boxes. Could include item boxes giving turbo mushrooms? But scope. Add "Turbo pads" and "boost orbs" perhaps collectible coins that fill boost. Coins scattered on track fill boost gauge. Nice.

HUD: lap counter, position (1st/6), speed km/h, boost gauge, minimap (canvas 2D showing track and karts), lap times, countdown 3-2-1-GO with engine rev, wrong-way indicator, results table.

Start screen overlay with title, kart color selection, controls, "PLAY". Could do full 3D attract camera orbit behind title. Simpler: game renders behind translucent start menu; camera orbits track. Kart selection with color swatches (6). Also choose difficulty? maybe not.

Countdown with race start: 3,2,1 GO; hold accelerate at right time? Rocket start if press accelerate during 2... maybe too complex. Add rocket start: pressing accelerate when "2" appears gives small boost. Nice.

Pause menu.

Results screen with placements and restart.

Mobile: touch controls visible when touch device; large buttons: left/right on bottom left, accelerate/brake and drift/boost on right. Layout via CSS media queries and pointer events. Also maybe auto-accelerate on mobile? Provide accelerate button.

Performance: three.js from vendor. Use fog, instanced meshes for trees/grass? Keep reasonable. Shadows: directional light shadow map maybe 2048; limited. Use PCFSoft. On mobile reduce pixel ratio. Bloom? Postprocessing requires addons; can avoid or vendor addons. Use simple emissive + sprites for glow. Could use EffectComposer/UnrealBloomPass but heavy in SwiftShader. Better no postprocessing; use additive glow sprites and fog.

Need screenshots and test in browser via playwright. Need run server. Static site: no package.json -> type html, default-start serves files. Port default 3000? Agents.md says open localhost:3002 Pascal dev server but default-start uses PORT env default 3000. We'll run start.sh with PORT=3002 maybe. capture script default may use 3002. Let's inspect start-project or env. Not needed; we'll run `PORT=3002 ./start.sh` in tmux (per Agents.md use persistent session). Use tmux availability. Then playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002, screenshot to screenshots/game.jpg (playwright screenshot may save png by extension? check options). We can also use node playwright script to capture JPEG 1280 wide. Instructions: save small JPEGs and read only latest. content.text:
playwright-cli screenshot [target]

screenshot of the current page or element

Arguments:
  [target]                    exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector
Options:
  --filename                  file name to save the screenshot to. defaults to `page-{timestamp}.{png|jpeg|webp}` if not specified.
  --type                      image format. if unset, inferred from the filename extension, otherwise png. (one of: png, jpeg, webp)
  --full-page                 when true, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport.
  --hires                     when true, captures a high-resolution screenshot using device pixels (accounts for the device pixel ratio), instead of css pixels.

Network works. Use npm to install three? Static html type can serve node_modules? start serves root; we can vendor `vendor/three.module.js` via npm install and copy. But if no package.json, default-start treats html and serves. We can create package.json with three dependency but projectType would throw unless vite. So don't create package.json; just download three.module.js to vendor. Use version 0.160.0 (or newer 0.187). Use r160 known API stable. Download. Maybe also GLTFLoader not needed.

Let's plan files:
- index.html
- styles.css
- js/main.js (module)
- vendor/three.module.js
Maybe split js into modules: track.js, kart.js, ai.js, audio.js, hud.js? Good engineering. Use ES modules with import map or direct import './vendor/three.module.js'. Simpler direct.

Need build high-quality visuals. Let me architect.

## Track

Define control points for a closed circuit. Let's design using 2D coordinate and elevation. Use CatmullRomCurve3 with centripetal? For closed curve, 'catmullrom' with tension 0.5. Sample 600 points, compute cumulative lengths, tangents, normals.

Track ribbon:
- For each sample i, point p, tangent t, side s = normalize(cross(up, t)) (right vector), bank maybe based on curvature for visual banking? Bank angle ~ clamp(curvature * speed factor), up vector rotates. For physics we can approximate flat up. Let's include banking for visual but karts also bank? Could complicate. Maybe small banking (max 8°) applied to road and karts. Height query from centerline enough.

Road width 16. Generate road geometry with 4 lateral strips? Road surface + curbs + shoulder.
- Road mesh with vertex colors? Use procedural texture repeated along V based on distance: asphalt with center dashed line, side lines. Texture mapping: U across width, V along length; canvas texture 256x256 with center line. Repeat V many times. Since width fixed, fine. Need UV v = distance / 12.
- Edge curbs: thin ribbons at ±(width/2 + 0.4) width 1.2, alternating red/white per segments. Could build two meshes with vertex colors alternating based on sample index groups. Use BufferGeometry with colors and MeshStandardMaterial vertexColors. Or segments as boxes every 2m. Ribbon easier.
- Shoulder grass: outer ribbon ±(width/2+1 to +6) green, maybe darker.
- Barriers? Add guardrails at some edges? Could add low walls/hedges around outer track to visually define. But collision only clamps; visual barrier not necessary everywhere. Use banners, tire stacks, trees.

Start/finish line: checkered strip across road at t=0, plus overhead arch with "TURBO KART" banner. Could create a gate: two pillars and banner. Need orient using frame.

Track furniture: 
- trees (cone+cylinder), colorful mushrooms (sphere cap + stem), palm trees, rocks, grandstands near start, balloons.
- turbo pads: glowing orange/blue chevrons on road at certain t values, width 5, length 4; when kart passes, boost impulse. Animate emissive.
- coin rings: golden coins (torus/cylinder) floating slightly above road at t offsets; collect adds boost. Rotate/bob.
- Item boxes? Maybe skip; coins fill turbo. Good.

Minimap: sample track points and draw.

## Physics

Player state:
- position Vector3, yaw angle, speed (m/s), lateral velocity? Use simplified kart:
  - throttle (0..1), brake, steer (-1..1), drift bool.
  - speed approaches maxSpeed with acceleration; offroad max lower.
  - yaw rate = steer * turnRate * f(speed) * (drifting ? 1.35 : 1), plus drift auto-turn.
  - position += forward * speed * dt; slight lateral drift when drifting (slip).
  - Find nearest sample by local search around previous index (trackIndex) for performance. Compute lateral offset = dot(pos - center, right). Clamp to road half width + shoulder. If beyond, offroad: reduce speed, dust particles. Actually clamp at road edge + 2 for shoulder? Let kart go on shoulder with slowdown; clamp at width/2+3.
  - Track y = center.y (plus maybe road thickness); kart y = track y.
  - Wrong way detection using dot(forward, tangent) < -0.3.

Speed: max 36 m/s (~130 km/h), boost 52 m/s (~187). Acceleration 16, brake 30, drag. Drift reduces top speed slightly but charges boost.

Drift:
- Press drift (Space) while steering and speed > 12: drifting true, builds charge from 0 to 1 over ~2.5s based on |steer|. Release: if charge > thresholds, mini-turbo boost duration & power based on tier. Blue sparks at >0.35, orange at >0.7, purple >1? Classic tiers.
- Boost gauge: fill from drifting (charge) and coins/pads. Press Shift or Turbo button: if gauge >= 25, activate boost 1.6s and drain 25. Boost adds acceleration and max speed, flames.
- Drift mini-turbo could also grant gauge. Use unified boost meter maybe. But request turbo: show gauge prominently, fill from drifting, coins, pads. Press Shift to use. On release of drift, auto mini-boost if charged enough without consuming gauge? Might overcomplicate. Design:
  - Drift charges "drift charge" separately; release gives mini-turbo (tiered) automatically.
  - Turbo gauge fills from drifting, coins, pads; press Shift to consume 33% for a strong boost.
  Both visual HUD: gauge with 3 segments? Show turbo meter and drift charge ring around speedometer.
  Hmm simpler and clearer: one "TURBO" meter. Drifting fills it. Press Shift to spend 30% for a 1.5s boost. Turbo pads give immediate speed boost + 20% meter; coins +8%. Drift release with full-ish charge also gives immediate mini-boost. Great.
- Boost state: boostTime, boostPower.

Kart visual:
- group with chassis etc. Update position/rotation from physics. Body roll = -steer*0.1 + drift lean. Wheel spin based on speed. Front wheels steer. Exhaust flame scale with boost.
- Shadow blob under kart? Use circle mesh with transparent texture; cheap.

AI:
- Each AI has track progress (t parameter distance), lateral target offset, speed. Use physics-ish movement along track: position follows centerline at distance s + lateral offset. They follow racing line with smooth lateral wander; target speed based on curvature ahead. This guarantees they stay on track and look natural. Add drift visual and occasional boost. Rubber band relative to player's progress.
- Need collision with player? Could add bumping: if distance < 3, push player sideways and slow. Nice but optional. Implement simple kart-kart collision (circle) for all karts with slight response. AI positions computed by track distance; player physical.
- Ranking: progress = lap * trackLength + s (player's s from nearest sample). Sort descending.
- Laps: crossing start line. For player track param: nearest sample distance; detect when previous s near end and new s near 0 -> lap++. AI increments s continuously mod length. For player easier use continuous progress: compute s; detect wrap. Handle backwards.
- Race: 3 laps; when player finishes, show results after AI finish? Let AI finish or simulate finishing. Show results overlay with times, restart. Could keep race running briefly; just end at player finish and compute positions by progress.

Camera:
- Third-person chase: target = kart pos + backward * 7 + up * 3.2, lookAt kart + forward*4 + up*1.4. Smooth lerp with speed-based FOV (60 -> 78). During boost FOV increases and shake. Start screen orbit camera.
- Intro countdown: camera behind kart.

Sky & environment:
- Sky shader gradient sphere or large sphere with vertex-color gradient; sun sprite, clouds as groups of white spheres low-poly, distant mountains (cones) and floating islands. Ground plane large with green gradient? Use a big plane with canvas texture subtle checker? Better large green plane with fog.
- Fog color matching horizon (light cyan/peach). Use hemisphere light + directional sun with shadows.
- Track raised above ground on low-poly terrain? If track has elevation, road floating. Build terrain mesh that follows track? Simpler: track mostly gentle elevation (0-12), ground plane at y=-1 with hills around. Road at y varying; add support "pillars" or embankments? Ribbon with skirts down to ground to look like solid road (side walls). Create skirts along both edges from road edge down 2.5m or to y=-1.5, giving thickness. For elevation, gaps maybe. Add underside dark. Could set track elevation modest (0-6) and add skirt 3m. Good.
- Add grass mounds/hills around track using low-poly spheres/cones; trees on them.
- Start grandstands: boxes with colored stripes and crowd dots (instanced small boxes?). Could be neat.

Textures:
- Road texture canvas 512x512: dark asphalt with noise, white dashed center line? In Mario Kart no center line necessarily; draw edge lines and start checkers separately. Road texture: asphalt speckle + subtle tire marks. Repeat along length 1x N? Set repeat(1, 40) maybe depends; use v based distance/8.
- Grass texture: canvas noise green; repeat 40.
- Checkered start line mesh: create plane across road with canvas checker.
- Banner textures with text "TURBO KART" / "TURBO GP" generated canvas. Need fonts available; use bold sans-serif.
- Coin texture? Use torus gold with emissive and rotation.

UI:
- Fonts: use Google Fonts? Offline safety; use system fonts with heavy italic styling. Could download a font? Maybe use CSS with 'Trebuchet MS', 'Arial Black'. For style, use Google Font "Baloo 2" or "Russo One" downloaded to assets? Network at runtime may not be guaranteed for viewers but likely. Better download woff2 for "Russo One" and maybe "Nunito". Use @font-face local. Let's download from Google Fonts via fonts.googleapis.com CSS. Russian text supported? Russo One supports Cyrillic I think. UI language Russian (request in Russian) — make Russian UI! Title "ТУРБО КАРТ", menu "ИГРАТЬ", controls "Газ", "Дрифт", "Турбо". Include Cyrillic font. Google font "Russo One" supports Cyrillic; "Rubik" supports Cyrillic. Download woff2 subsets? Google Fonts CSS with `subset=cyrillic`? Simpler download variable font from GitHub? Could use @import Google fonts; offline might fail. Let's fetch CSS and woff2 (latin+cyrillic). Use Rubik (400-900) for UI and Russo One for headings. Check.

- HUD layout: top-left position + lap; top-center lap time / best; top-right minimap; bottom-left speedometer (circular gauge) with boost meter; bottom-right controls hint; boost gauge near speed. Mobile controls overlaid bottom.
- Start overlay: big logo with gradient, kart color swatches, controls, start button; background game scene blurred/dim.
- Countdown big numbers with scale animation.
- Results table.
- Pause overlay.

Audio:
- WebAudio synth engine: oscillator sawtooth + gain, pitch based on speed; boost noise; countdown beeps; coin chime; drift skid noise; crowd? Keep manageable. Mute button. Initialize on start. Engine sound loop with two oscillators and lowpass. Update frequency. Boost adds noise. Implement AudioManager.

## Implementation details

Three.js version r160 import. Need to ensure WebGL works in SwiftShader headed Chromium. Yes.

Use renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({antialias:true, powerPreference:'high-performance'}); setPixelRatio(min(devicePixelRatio, 2)); shadowMap enabled PCFSoft; toneMapping ACESFilmic; outputColorSpace SRGB.

Scene scale: track ~300m. Camera far 1200.

Track control points. Let's design coordinates carefully. Use a circuit in XZ. Let's sketch a fun shape with varied turns and elevation. We'll compute curvature and validate.

Option: Use 12-14 points:
P0 (0, 2, 60) start/finish heading +x? Let's make start straight along +x at z=60.
P1 (70, 2, 55)
P2 (120, 3, 25) sweeping right? 
P3 (135, 6, -30) 
P4 (105, 9, -85)
P5 (45, 8, -105)
P6 (0, 5, -75) hairpin? 
P7 (-40, 4, -110)
P8 (-105, 6, -95)
P9 (-140, 3, -40)
P10 (-125, 0, 15)
P11 (-75, 0, 55)
P12 (-25, 1, 65)
closed.

Check min distances. It's a loop around perimeter; likely okay. Need start straight; P0->P1 ~70. Start at t=0 at P0? Curve passes control points; start/finish at P0. Start line tangent roughly +x. But camera behind looking +x.

Elevation changes: gentle. Could add hill at P4/P5. Use y values.

Maybe include a bridge/tunnel? Scope maybe skip. A tunnel would be cool but complex. Add a jump? Not necessary.

Add an "S" section: P6 at (5,5,-72) then P7 (-45,4,-105) creates S. Good.

Hairpin at P2/P3 maybe sweeping.

Road width 18 to allow overtakes. Length ~800m. 3 laps ~2.4km; at 130 km/h ~1.5 min. Good.

Track sampling:
- curve.getSpacedPoints(1200) for even spacing? getSpacedPoints uses arc length; yes. Compute lengths via distance.
- frame at each sample: tangent = normalize(p[i+1]-p[i-1]); right = normalize(cross(tangent, up)); up2 = cross(right,tangent) for banking.
- banking: curvature from tangent change; bank = clamp(curvatureSigned * k, -0.15, 0.15) applied? Might complicate. Skip banking, but road can tilt with "up" constant. Elevation gives interest.

Road geometry: positions at p ± right*width/2, y = p.y. Add slight crown? skip. Use MeshStandardMaterial map road texture, roughness .9, metalness 0. Color. Need polygonOffset for decals.

UV: u 0/1 across, v = distance/6 for repeat. Texture repeat wrapping. Actually set texture.repeat(1,1) and bake v multiples; UV values beyond 1 wrap. Fine.

Curbs: strips at [halfWidth, halfWidth+1.4] with alternating colors. To alternate along segments, create separate quads per sample segment colored by floor(i/6)%2. That's 1200 segments * 2 sides * 2 tris = manageable. Use vertex colors with MeshStandardMaterial vertexColors. Also add outer white line? Road texture includes edge lines maybe.

Skirt walls: from edge x=halfWidth+1.4 down to y-2.8, dark gray. Also underside not needed.

Grass shoulders: ribbon from halfWidth+1.4 to +7, green texture. But if the terrain plane is below, shoulders floating; skirts cover. Could skip shoulder ribbon and let ground show. But track elevated; add green apron around edges for blending: from edge to +5 with same y-0.2. Then skirt from apron edge down 3m. Looks like floating track island; okay stylized. Use "grass" material.

Terrain: big plane at y=-2 with green; plus hills. Track skirt to y=-3.

Start gate: at s=0, create group oriented along tangent. Pillars at ±(width/2+2), height 9, banner box across width+4 at y 9. Canvas texture "TURBO KART" checkered. Also checkered start strip 2m long across road (plane y+0.02).

Turbo pads at s values: 90, 260, 430, 620, 720 maybe. Each: a plane 6 wide 5 long with animated chevron texture (canvas arrows), emissive orange, plus glow. Rotation aligned to tangent. Need place on road surface. Use canvas texture with arrows, additive? MeshBasicMaterial with transparent map, blending additive, depthWrite false. Under it a solid pad. Trigger when player progress within ±2.5m and lateral <4; boost. AI too (visual speed). Cooldown per pad.

Coins: positions at various s, lateral offsets, y+1.2; ring of 5 coins maybe. Rotating gold cylinders with coin texture? Use CylinderGeometry(0.45,0.45,0.1,16) rotated so face visible? Coins stand upright like Mario coins: cylinder axis Z? Cylinder default axis Y; rotate X 90° to stand vertical facing along track. Better use a flat cylinder rotated so its face points sideways? Mario coins spin around Y. Use Torus? Let's make coin as cylinder radius .45 height .08, rotate Z 90? If axis Y and thin height, it's a horizontal disc; viewed from behind edge-on. Rotate around X by 90 -> vertical disc facing forward. Then spin around Y for glint. Add emissive gold. Group bob and rotate. Collection radius 2.2; +8% turbo, chime, sparkle.

Trees: generate along both sides at sample intervals with random offsets outside track (>= width/2+8), y from ground? If track elevated, placing on ground y=-2 would be far below. Place trees relative to track height at nearby sample but offset outward, so on apron level, looks okay. Use y = p.y - 0.5 at offset, with trunk. Since apron extends 5m, trees at +8..20 hover? The ground plane at y=-2, so at offset 15 there's no support
